MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND
  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION JOINT MEETING
  CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING
  OCTOBER 22, 2019

A joint adjourned meeting of the Rolling Hills Estates City Council and Park & Activities
Commission was called to order by MAYOR MITCHELL at 5:35 p.m. in the Council Chamber at
Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan*, Zuckerman
  *Arrived at 5:50 p.m.
City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz.

Commission Member Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, Romanelli, Van Ingen-Pope

Commission Members Absent:  McCormick, Persichina, Retz

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

OVERVIEW OF 2019 CITY CELEBRATION – VICE CHAIR LOU PERSICHINA

VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA was not present to provide the overview.

DISCUSSION ITEM

A.  2019 CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING REPORT

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho presented the debrief report for the 62nd
  Annual City Celebration held on September 21, 2019 at Empty Saddle Club, starting with
  the venue, and reviewed the venue suggestions for next year’s City Celebration which
  included:

  •  Provide shade for the picnic area
  •  Provide additional parking

  Discussion ensued concerning the issues related to shade and parking. To address the
  issues raised, the group made the following suggestions:

  •  Provide shuttle service for the PV Symphonic band members
  •  Allow street parking on Empty Saddle
  •  Provide shade for the picnic area and performance stage

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL/P&A MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 22, 2019 (CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING)
   Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided an overview of the general event details
  and reported that there were approximately 1,500 attendees compared to 800 last year. He
  stated that in reviewing dates for next year’s City Celebration, staff has found either
  September 19 or 26 could be suitable dates as they do not conflict with either the USC or
  UCLA home football games. He further noted the following suggestions for next year’s
  event:

  •  Additional seating for entertainment audience
  •  Three cakes instead of four
  •  Improve food quality
  •  Increase quantity of food

  Discussion ensued concerning options for improving the quality and quantity of food. It was
  noted that the reason that the food ran out could have been due to the increase in
  attendance over last year.

  In response to a suggestion that food trucks be incorporated as an additional food option,
  it was the concurrence of the group that the Empty Saddle Club be given another
  opportunity to provide the food with better direction as to menu options and quantity of food
  needed. The group also concurred that it would be a good addition to have an ice
  cream/treat truck present at the event as an additional food option.

  Discussion ensued concerning the pros and cons of the Equestrian Committee’s
  suggestion that a separate dinner be added to the event. The group decided that a dinner
  should not be added given that attendance dwindles in the late afternoon and it would
  increase the cost of the event.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a recap of the entertainment and
  activities. A general discussion was held regarding the event activities, ticket sales and
  music options, with some of the suggestions being as follows:
  •  Accept credit cards for games and meal tickets
  •  Continue using Los Hermanos as volunteer base
  •  Coordinate timing of events better so events don’t compete with each other
  •  Move DJ closer to kids area so announcements can be heard
  •  Keep community booths
  •  PV Symphonic Band – ask band to add country western music (donation required)
  •  Look into adding a country/western band
  •  Focus on increasing revenue from local businesses and organizations
  •  Charge flat fee for a wrist band for participation in all equestrian events to increase
  participation
  •  Secure prizes for poker ride earlier next year
  •  Extend activities hours to 3:00 p.m.; possibly begin at 9:00 a.m.
  •  Research adding additional activities ie: rock climbing wall
  •  Require ticket for face painting
  •  Add a second corn kernel box (with age restrictions)

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL/P&A MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 22, 2019 (CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING)
   •  Eliminate hay jumping pit.
  •  Stick horse races were popular but should be moved to grass area
  •  Continue Home Depot craft activity

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja reviewed the event promotions noting that the
  direct mailer sent to all residents was sent at a lower cost this year because the mailing
  services was not used. Discussion ensued concerning the promotions with the following
  suggestions being made:

  •  Increase promotion on social media
  •  Eliminate ad in Peninsula People
  •  Have vendors collect free tickets sent to residents as a gauge for effectiveness of
  the direct mailer
  •  Modify sponsorship package opportunities; add annual sponsorship options
  •  Goal for next year $7,500 in sponsorship

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho reviewed the financial summary. A general
  discussion ensued concerning ways to increase sponsorship and provide a better
  experience for the attendees.

  Following discussion, there was a general consensus that next year’s event be held on
  Saturday, September 26, 2019 at the Empty Saddle Club.

ADJOURNMENT

At 6:37 p.m. MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the meeting to the next regular meeting of the City
Council scheduled to be held on Tuesday, November 12, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. and the next regular
meeting of the Park & Activities Commission scheduled to be held Monday, November 18, 2019
beginning at 7:00 p.m. Both meetings will be held in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates
City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL/P&A MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 22, 2019 (CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING)
